fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Procurement, Technical Specialist, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Annual assortment review or new solar technology market entry
fields.Volume: ~200–300 solar SKUs across panels, inverters, batteries, mounting, wiring

workflows.name: Solar Product Assortment Planning & Vendor Selection

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Category Manager reviews solar market trends" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-import of "Procurement sources and qualifies solar vendors" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-create of "creates planogram for dedicated solar display area" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-439 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Product Merchandising & Consultation (PA-70.1).)
- operational: Category Manager — Electrical review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rapid technology evolution**: Solar panel efficiency improves 1–2% annually; SKU obsolescence risk
- **Import dependency**: 90%+ solar products imported; supply chain disruption risk
System Touchpoints: - Item master with solar-specific attributes (wattage, efficiency rating, certifications)
- Vendor qualification workflow with technical certification tracking
- Assortment planning module with store-tier matrix

steps.activity: Category Manager reviews solar market trends: panel technology (mono PERC, bifacial, half-cut), inverter types (string vs. micro), battery storage, EV charging integration; identifies 20–30 new SKUs for introduction; evaluates vendor certifications (TÜV, IEC, UL)

Procurement sources and qualifies solar vendors: Philippines product certification (BPS/DTI), ERC registration, warranty terms, technical support capability, lead time for panels (import: 45–60 days); negotiates volume rebates and co-marketing funds

Merchandising finalizes assortment matrix: Tier 1 stores (Metro Manila, Cebu, Davao) carry full solar range; Tier 2 stores carry core packages; online carries complete catalog; creates planogram for dedicated solar display area (minimum 16 sqm)

fields.Participants: Dept Supervisor, Solar-Trained Sales Associate, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer inquiry about solar installation at store or via ecommerce
fields.Volume: ~1–2 per store per week at Tier 1 stores; ~2–4 per month at Tier 2

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enters data into ERP solar sizing tool" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "count, inverter sizing, battery backup requirement" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-create of "creates sales order with installation option" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-439 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Product Merchandising & Consultation (PA-70.1).)
- operational: site survey verification; operational: fails to deliver promised savings
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incorrect sizing**: Undersized system fails to deliver promised savings; mitigated by site survey verification
- **Customer expectation management**: ROI estimates depend on future electricity rates and actual solar irradiance
System Touchpoints: - Solar sizing calculator integrated with ERP product catalog and pricing
- Quotation generation with bundle pricing for solar kits
- CRM lead capture with solar pipeline stage
- Installation service scheduling integration

steps.activity: Sales Associate conducts needs assessment: customer monthly electricity bill (kWh), roof type and orientation, available roof area, current electrical panel capacity, shading analysis; enters data into ERP solar sizing tool

System generates recommended solar system size: calculates panel count, inverter sizing, battery backup requirement; produces estimated ROI (payback period typically 3–5 years in Philippines); generates preliminary quotation

Customer selects configuration; Associate creates sales order with installation option; if installation requested, schedules site survey with certified solar installer partner; captures lead in CRM for follow-up

fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Pricing Analyst, Merchandising, Procurement
fields.Trigger: New product introduction or seasonal promotion

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Pricing Analyst calculates bundle pricing" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-scan of "System configures kit/bundle in ERP" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Component mismatch**: Kit components from different vendors may have compatibility issues
- **Inventory synchronization**: Kit availability depends on all component availability
System Touchpoints: - Kit/bundle master with BOM component linking
- Pricing engine with bundle discount rules
- POS bundle barcode configuration

steps.activity: Category Manager designs solar packages by system size: 1kW (basic household), 3kW (standard), 5kW (medium), 10kW (large household/small business); each bundle includes panels, inverter, mounting kit, cables, breakers, and installation labor SKU
Pricing Analyst calculates bundle pricing: component cost + 5–10% bundle discount vs. individual items; verifies margin targets (25–30%); compares against competitor solar package pricing in market

System configures kit/bundle in ERP: links component SKUs to parent bundle, defines BOM, sets assembly lead time (if pre-assembled), configures POS bundle scanning; tests at pilot store before rollout

fields.Trigger: Monthly pricing review or Meralco/DU rate change

workflows.name: Solar Product Pricing & Net Metering ROI Calculator

Automation Opportunity: - System rule-based auto-approval of "approved net metering rates, average solar irradiance per region" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews solar product pricing vs." (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "generates updated sales collateral with revised savings estimates" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-439 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Product Merchandising & Consultation (PA-70.1).)
- operational: Pricing Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rate volatility**: DU rate changes affect ROI calculations; stale data misleads customers
- **Regulatory changes**: Net metering rules may change under ERC
System Touchpoints: - ROI calculator engine with DU rate database
- Multi-channel price sync
- Pricing analytics with competitive benchmarking

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst updates ROI calculator parameters: current utility rates per DU (Meralco, Davao Light, VECO, etc.), ERC-approved net metering rates, average solar irradiance per region (5–5.5 kWh/m²/day in Philippines), panel degradation rate (0.5%/year), system cost trends

Analyst reviews solar product pricing vs. competitors and online market; adjusts pricing to maintain target margin while ensuring ROI calculator shows <5 year payback for standard systems; flags SKUs where cost increase threatens payback threshold
System updates pricing and ROI calculator across all channels (in-store kiosk, ecommerce, mobile app); generates updated sales collateral with revised savings estimates

fields.Participants: Training Mgr, Category Manager, Solar Vendor Trainers, Sales Associates
fields.Trigger: New product launch, new hire, or annual recertification
fields.Volume: ~400–600 solar-certified associates across 200 stores (2–3 per store)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "technology basics, inverter selection, battery sizing, Philippine electrical code…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "profile" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks certification status in employee profile" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Training attrition**: Solar-certified staff turnover requires continuous retraining
- **Knowledge depth**: 8-hour training may be insufficient for complex consultation scenarios
System Touchpoints: - LMS with solar certification tracking
- Employee profile with certification badge

steps.activity: Training Manager develops solar product curriculum with vendor support: panel technology basics, inverter selection, battery sizing, Philippine electrical code compliance, net metering process, safety protocols, customer consultation methodology

Delivery: online modules via LMS (4 hours) + in-store practical workshop with vendor demo units (4 hours); associates must pass certification quiz (80% minimum); certified associates receive badge on name tag and ERP profile

HR tracks certification status in employee profile; Store Managers ensure minimum 2 certified associates per store; recertification required annually; uncategorized associates cannot sell solar systems

fields.Participants: Supply Planner, Procurement, DC Ops, Category Manager
fields.Trigger: Monthly inventory review or stockout incident

workflows.name: Solar Product Inventory & Lead Time Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews solar inventory levels vs." (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approves SKU substitution at store level" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "DC Ops ensures special handling for solar panels" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-439 (ensure controlled execution — Solar Product Merchandising & Consultation (PA-70.1).)
- operational: Supply Planner review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Long lead times**: Solar panel imports from China/Taiwan; seasonal demand spikes exceed buffer stock
- **Product damage**: Solar panels are fragile; transport damage rate ~2–3% requires vendor claims process
System Touchpoints: - Inventory planning with extended lead time parameters for solar imports
- ATP check considering import vessel schedules
- WMS special handling instructions for fragile/highbay items

steps.activity: Supply Planner reviews solar inventory levels vs. demand forecast: panels (high volume, import, 45–60 day lead time), inverters (medium volume, import, 30–45 days), mounting kits (local, 14 days), batteries (growing demand, import, 30–60 days); adjusts safety stock for A-items at 3 weeks vs. standard 1–2 weeks

For stockout or low-stock critical items: Procurement expedites with vendor; explores air freight for high-margin items; identifies substitute products; Category Manager approves SKU substitution at store level

DC Ops ensures special handling for solar panels: vertical storage racks, fragile handling protocols, dedicated staging area for large orders; coordinates consolidated delivery with customer installation schedule

steps.activity: Sales Associate captures lead in CRM: customer contact, electricity consumption data, property details, system interest level, budget range; assigns lead source (in-store, online, referral, trade account)

Solar Sales Coordinator qualifies lead: contacts customer within 24 hours, confirms requirements, schedules site survey with installation partner, sends preliminary quotation; updates CRM pipeline stage (New → Qualified → Site Survey → Quoted)

Coordinator manages pipeline: follows up quoted leads within 7 days, nurtures cold leads with monthly solar education content, reports conversion metrics (lead-to-sale target: 15–20%), escalates large commercial leads (>20kW) to Category Manager
